wtb.label: Wheel, Tire & Brakes
wtb.spec: Same wheel and tire all round · brakes differ front to rear

tire.label: Tire
tire.brand: Pirelli P Zero AS Plus 3 replacement option
tire.where: All four corners — same size front and rear
tire.spec: 275/40R20 106Y XL · 9–11 in approved rim range and 2,094 lb max load · confirm the door placard and every installed sidewall
tire.stock: Discount Tire · direct product page live when reviewed
tire.dueNote: You are 25,000 mi past a typical set.
tire.issue: Heat-cycled sidewalls on a 392 go off well before the tread does — a set that still shows tread can be long past its grip.

wheelA.label: Wheel
wheelA.where: All four corners — same part front and rear
wheelA.life: Inspect for curb damage and runout at every rotation

lugs.label: Lug Nuts
lugs.life: Replace any nut that no longer takes a 22 mm socket cleanly
lugs.issue: Classic Chrysler swollen-lug-nut failure — the chrome cap separates and balloons, so the socket won't seat. Extremely common by 60k. Solid one-piece aftermarket nuts are the usual fix.

tpms.label: TPMS Sensor
tpms.where: Inside the wheel at the valve stem
tpms.life: Battery is sealed — 7 to 10 years, then the whole sensor

frontBrakes.label: Front Brakes
frontBrakes.life: The end that does 70% of the stopping — and wears like it

rearBrakes.label: Rear Brakes
rearBrakes.life: Rears typically go two front sets before they need anything

brakeFluid.label: Brake Fluid
brakeFluid.where: Master cylinder reservoir, driver side firewall
brakeFluid.spec: DOT 4 only · 1.0 qt for a full flush · dry boiling point 509 °F
brakeFluid.life: Flush every 2 years or 30,000 mi — it absorbs water whether you drive or not
brakeFluid.issue: Old fluid boils under repeated hard stops and the pedal goes long right when you need it — the cheapest brake job on the list.

caliper.label: Front Caliper
caliper.life: Rebuild or replace when a piston sticks or a boot tears

rotor.label: Front Rotor
rotor.spec: 390 × 34 mm · SRT 392 six-piston Brembo branch · replace as an axle pair
rotor.life: Inspect thickness, runout, cracks and heat damage. Follow the rotor maker’s minimum thickness and resurfacing limits; replace as an axle pair when outside limits.
rotor.issue: Front rotors on the 392 warp early if the car sees hard street stops. Watch for steering-wheel shudder at 55–65 mph braking.

pads.label: Front Pads
pads.brand: Genuine Mopar six-piston front disc brake pad kit
pads.spec: BR7 six-piston SRT 392 front brakes only. Confirm the installed calipers; the BR4 four-piston 68144213 pad family is not interchangeable.
pads.life: 30k–45k on a 392 driven the way a 392 gets driven
pads.dueNote: 20,000 mi past a typical front set.
pads.issue: Pad slap and a low pedal are the tells on this car long before the wear sensor squeals.

caliperR.label: Rear Caliper
caliperR.life: Inspect piston movement, seals, dust boots and pad-retaining hardware during brake service. This is a fixed caliper, not a sliding-caliper design.

rotorR.label: Rear Rotor
rotorR.spec: 350 mm SRT rear-brake branch · replace as an axle pair
rotorR.life: Usually outlives two front sets — replace in pairs when they do go

padsR.label: Rear Pads
padsR.brand: Genuine Mopar rear disc brake pad kit
padsR.spec: BR4 four-piston SRT rear branch · not interchangeable with the fronts

oilFluid.label: Engine Oil
oilFluid.life: 6,000 mi or 6 months, whichever lands first
oilFluid.issue: The 392 is one of the few HEMIs that genuinely needs 0W-40 — a quick-lube 5W-20 fill is how lifters start ticking.

oilFilter.label: Oil Filter
oilFilter.spec: 6.4L HEMI fitment · lubricate the gasket and follow the filter installation instructions

oilPlug.label: Drain Plug & Gasket
oilPlug.life: Inspect the plug and sealing surface at every oil change. Replace damaged hardware and any seal the exact service procedure identifies as single-use.

wipL.label: Driver Blade
wipL.issue: Chattering and streaking on the driver side is the most common wiper complaint on this car — the arm spring weakens before the rubber goes.

wipR.label: Passenger Blade
wipR.life: Replace as a pair with the driver blade

wipFluid.label: Washer Fluid
wipFluid.spec: Do not use plain water — the pump freezes

eng.label: Engine
eng.life: Oil, filters and coolant are the whole maintenance story on this engine

airFilter.label: Engine Air Filter
airFilter.spec: 6.4L SRT HEMI branch · dry replacement element · do not wash or oil
airFilter.life: Every 30,000 mi, sooner on dirt roads
airFilter.issue: A loaded filter on a 392 shows up as a lazy top end long before any code sets.

cabinFilter.label: Cabin Air Filter
cabinFilter.where: Fresh-air inlet below the cowl access cover
cabinFilter.spec: 2015 Challenger all-engine branch · install in the airflow direction shown on the element
cabinFilter.issue: This is the one people notice — weak vents and a musty smell on first start.

radCore.label: Radiator
radCore.issue: 2011–2021 Challenger, all trims — the crimped plastic end tanks split at the seams and weep, typically between 60,000 and 100,000 mi and sooner on a 392 driven hard or in heat. Symptoms start as a seam leak, low-coolant warnings and steam under load.
radCore.issueRef: OEM radiator premature failure · 2011–2021 · all trims · 35 owner reports

upgrade.label: Mishimoto MMRAD-SRT-15
upgrade.fixes: Replaces the original plastic end tanks with welded aluminium tanks. Diagnose the leak first; an upgraded radiator can still develop leaks or other cooling faults.
upgrade.fit: Reviewed for the 2015 Challenger SRT 392. Confirm the installed cooling configuration before ordering; do not extend this check to other engines or model years.

node.spec: 2-row aluminium core · 1.96-inch core thickness · welded tanks. Check the installation instructions and correct cap separately; a cap pressure is not established by this product review.
node.life: Condition-based inspection. Follow the manufacturer’s warranty terms; a warranty is not a guarantee against future cooling faults.
node.resolved: Upgrade recorded. Confirm the original leak is repaired and the cooling system passes its post-repair checks.

radCore.where: Front of the engine bay, behind the grille
radCore.spec: 6.4L SRT HEMI branch · verify VIN and severe-duty cooling configuration
radCore.life: Inspect the tank seams at every coolant change — the plastic end tanks are what fail, not the core

radOem.label: OEM · plastic end tanks
radOem.where: Front of the engine bay, behind the grille
radOem.spec: 6.4L SRT HEMI branch · aluminium core with crimped plastic tanks
radOem.life: Condition-based replacement, not a fixed mileage deadline. Inspect for coolant loss, seam leaks, corrosion and overheating; diagnose the cooling system before replacing the radiator.
radOem.issue: This is the part the known issue is written about. A like-for-like replacement resets the clock but keeps the failure mode.
radOem.issueRef: OEM radiator premature failure · 2011–2021 · all trims

coolant.label: Antifreeze
coolant.where: Reservoir on the passenger side of the radiator

coolant.life: 10 years or 150,000 mi from new, then every 5 years

oilPlug.label: Drain Plug & Gasket

trx.label: Transmission

transFluid.label: Transmission Fluid
transFluid.where: Fill plug on the driver side of the pan — filled from underneath
transFluid.spec: Set the level using the exact temperature procedure · never substitute ATF+4
transFluid.life: 60,000 mi for this owner-facing plan; shorten for track or tow use
transFluid.dueNote: 5,000 mi past due — never logged on this demo car.

transPan.label: Pan & Filter
transPan.spec: Pan, filter and gasket are serviced as one assembly · automatic 8HP70 only; confirm VIN
transPan.life: Replace with a full automatic-transmission fluid service

transPlug.label: Fill Plug Seal
transPlug.where: Fill plug on the transmission pan
transPlug.spec: Use the exact service procedure and torque for the installed transmission
transPlug.life: Replace whenever the fill plug is removed
